doors.trait: Your rules outlive the reasons for them, and you enforce them anyway. Gym at six, lunch at noon, lights out at eleven, held through a fever and a friend’s one free evening in town. The structure was built to serve you. Somewhere it quietly reversed.
doors.scene: A friend was in town for one evening, the first in three years. Lights out at eleven held anyway, the way it held through the fever, the way it holds through everything. You slept on schedule and lay there knowing exactly what the schedule had cost.
doors.outside: People plan around your routine the way they plan around weather, and they stopped asking for exceptions years ago. The discipline earns real respect. What nobody mentions is how rarely you appear in the stories they tell about their best nights.
